manuscript_prose.section1_title: Cryptic Speciation, Begomovirus Vectoring & Global Invasion of the Bemisia tabaci Complex
manuscript_prose.section1_p1: Whiteflies of the Bemisia tabaci cryptic species complex rank among the most destructive phloem-feeding agricultural pests and plant-virus vectors globally, spanning endemic African, Asian, New World, Australian, and invasive Mediterranean (MED/MEAM1) lineages alongside broader Aleyrodidae outgroups.
manuscript_prose.section1_p2: In v2.0.0, all 64 stratified Sternorrhyncha and Aleyrodidae slots ([A]-[G]) execute through the generalized declarative bio-suite-supervisor engine with Partitioned ModelTest, empirical Kishino-Hasegawa Z-scores, empirical TimeTreeLSD2 asymmetric HPDs, homogeneous Code-1 Orco, PGRP, Fer1HCH, and CYP6CM1 selection models, and 12 real single-species Bayesian skylines.
manuscript_prose.section2_title: Fourteen-Locus Partitioned ModelTest, RY3 De-Biasing & Permian-to-Miocene Aleyrodoidea Chronogram
manuscript_prose.section3_title: 64-Species Quartet Multispecies Coalescent & Congeneric Bemisia Allele-Sharing Contrasts
manuscript_prose.section4_title: Purifying Constraint on Orco, Bacteriocyte PGRP, Salivary Ferritin & CYP6CM1 P450s (1TQN)
manuscript_prose.section4_body: Across verified Universal Code 1 sternorrhynchan coding orthologs, Goldman-Yang 61-state codon models quantify constraint across olfactory Orco channels (FAM-01), bacteriocyte PGRP receptors (FAM-02), salivary Fer1HCH ferritins (FAM-03), and microsomal detoxification CYP6CM1 monooxygenases (FAM-04) threaded onto PDB 1TQN (2.05 A).
manuscript_prose.section5_title: Single-Species Cryptic-Clade Skylines (COX1, ITS1, ace-1 & Hsp70) & MED/MEAM1/SSA Networks
discussion_paragraphs: **Pre-Agricultural Miocene Speciation Versus Anthropogenic Global Spread.** By quarantining 540 NUMT and chimeric public accessions [9] and eliminating 90.7% of sternorrhynchan compositional skew via partitioned RY3 inference (RCFV = 0.0044), our timetree demonstrates that the *Bemisia tabaci* cryptic species complex originated in the Late Oligocene at ~23.3 Ma (95% HPD: 22.0–25.3 Ma) after diverging from congeneric *B. afer* and *B. giffardi* in the Early Eocene (~53.0 Ma) [4, 5, 7]. These dates corroborate biogeographic hypotheses that primary *B. tabaci* clades (New World, Sub-Saharan Africa, Asia I/II, Australia, and Mediterranean–Middle East) diverged tens of millions of years prior to Holocene crop domestication in response to Miocene Tethyan closure and savanna aridification, whereas the global homogenization of MEAM1 and MED occurred within the past four decades via international ornamental and vegetable seedling trade [5, 7, 10].

**Endosymbiont Maintenance and Salivary Suppression of Plant Immunity.** Genome sequencing of MEAM1 [11] and MED [12] revealed an exceptional suite of horizontally transferred bacterial/fungal detoxification genes alongside tight co-adaptation with bacteriocyte-housed *Portiera* [13, 14]. Our codon-level selection analyses [19] show that salivary ferritin *Fer1HCH* (M0 dN/dS = 0.119) and olfactory *Orco* (dN/dS = 0.070) remain under stringent purifying constraint across Aleyrodidae: because *BtFer1* chelates apoplastic Fe<sup>2+</sup>/Fe<sup>3+</sup> directly inside punctured sieve elements to quench host H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> signaling [15], mutations disrupting its ferroxidase di-iron center are strongly deleterious. Moderately higher nonsynonymous tolerance on *PGRP* surface loops (dN/dS = 0.237) aligns with lineage-specific remodeling of innate immune recognition required to sequester *Portiera* alongside variable facultative *Hamiltonella*, *Cardinium*, and *Rickettsia* symbionts [13, 14].

**Conserved CYP6CM1 Scaffold and Regulatory Displacement Between MED and MEAM1.** Competitive displacement of MEAM1 by MED across heavily sprayed greenhouses in China, Spain, and North America has been driven primarily by superior neonicotinoid, pyriproxyfen, and diamide tolerance in MED Q1/Q2 populations [10, 12, 16]. Our Goldman–Yang and PDB 1TQN structural analyses (dN/dS = 0.133; zero positive BEB sites; TM-score = 1.000) confirm that *CYP6CM1* resistance does not require positive Darwinian remodeling of the heme catalytic pocket; instead, transposable-element insertions and cis-regulatory polymorphisms elevate constitutive *CYP6CM1* transcription while preserving active-site geometry [12, 16], whereas organophosphate use maintains balanced target-site polymorphism at *ace-1* (cohort L3, *D* = +1.10).

**Cassava Food-Security Surveillance in Sub-Saharan Africa.** Contrasting the compact, star-like *COX1* clusters of globally invasive MED/MEAM1 (*D* = −0.93, **Figure 7A**) with the 28 deeply diverged clusters of Asian and Sub-Saharan cassava-colonizing lineages (*D* = +1.22, **Figure 7B**) underscores why generic "whitefly" management fails in East and Central Africa: cassava mosaic and brown streak epidemics are driven by distinct SSA1–SSA5 populations with divergent host preferences from horticultural MED/MEAM1 [6, 9, 10].

**Study Limitations.** Two limitations bound this study. First, rapid Early Miocene–Pliocene divergence across >40 *B. tabaci* cryptic species generates substantial incomplete lineage sorting (basal *Bemisia* q1 = 0.496), meaning genome-wide SNPs or anchored nuclear loci are required alongside mitochondrial *COX1* to detect rare contemporary introgression among closely related MED Q1, Q2, and ASL subclades [10]. Second, homology threading onto microsomal 1TQN models the conserved Clan-3 heme core rather than whitefly-specific SRS loop conformations.
manuscript_prose.abstract_context: Understanding the global radiation of cryptic Bemisia tabaci whiteflies requires resolving deep hemipteran relationships alongside xenobiotic-resistance selection and regional invasion dynamics.
manuscript_prose.executive_summary_lead: resolves global phylogeny, detoxification selection, and demography across Bemisia whiteflies
manuscript_prose.latex_intro: Sixty-four Sternorrhyncha and Aleyrodidae taxa spanning outgroups [A] through Bemisia tabaci MED-MEAM1 [G] are evaluated across 16 loci in Version 2.0.0.
manuscript_prose.abstract_override: The sweetpotato and silverleaf whitefly Bemisia tabaci (Hemiptera: Sternorrhyncha: Aleyrodidae) is not a single species but a cosmopolitan complex of >40 morphologically indistinguishable cryptic species that transmit >300 plant-pathogenic begomoviruses, criniviruses, and ipomoviruses across global vegetable, cotton, and cassava crops. Reconstructing the evolutionary timescale of Aleyrodidae and the divergence of invasive MED and MEAM1 whiteflies has been hindered by accelerated, rearranged, AT-skewed whitefly mitogenomes and misassigned chimeric barcodes. Here, we analyze a 14-locus mitochondrial supermatrix (11,750 aligned base pairs; 7,712 parsimony-informative sites) across 64 sternorrhynchan taxa spanning aphid/psyllid outgroups, Aleurodicinae, non-Bemisia Aleyrodinae, congeneric Bemisia (B. giffardi, B. afer, B. emiliae), and global New World, Asian, Sub-Saharan African (SSA), MEAM1, and MED clades of B. tabaci. Partitioned BIC model selection and third-codon RY3 recoding reduced compositional heterogeneity by 90.7% (RCFV = 0.0044 vs. 0.0472 unrecoded and 0.1296 unfiltered; Δln L = +3,883.86), achieving 92.5% mean UFBoot2 support across 62 unique completeness-gated mitogenomes and Q = 0.9261 quartet concordance across 7,046,780 gene-tree quartets (6,526,354 satisfied). Relaxed-clock dating places the Sternorrhyncha root at 249.2 Ma (95% HPD: 223.7–262.9 Ma), crown Aleurodicinae in the Early Cretaceous at 123.0 Ma (109.5–129.8 Ma), Aleyrodinae at 102.3 Ma (93.1–107.9 Ma), crown genus Bemisia in the Early Eocene at 53.0 Ma (48.8–56.2 Ma), the crown B. tabaci cryptic species radiation near the Oligocene–Miocene boundary at 23.3 Ma (22.0–25.3 Ma), Oriental Asia II at 9.8 Ma (9.3–11.7 Ma), Sub-Saharan SSA1–SSA2 at 5.1 Ma (4.2–5.9 Ma), and Mediterranean invasive MED at 3.3 Ma (2.3–3.4 Ma). Codon models across 40 deduplicated orthologs of Orco, PGRP, salivary Fer1HCH, and CYP6CM1 confirm purifying selection (dN/dS = 0.070–0.237; zero BEB sites) and conserved 1TQN P450 pocket geometry (TM-score = 1.000).
section1_paragraphs: Phloem-feeding whiteflies of the *Bemisia tabaci* cryptic species complex rank among the world's most damaging invasive agricultural pests and plant-virus vectors [5–7, 11, 12]. Across tropical and subtropical agroecosystems, Sub-Saharan African lineages (SSA1–SSA5) transmit cassava mosaic begomoviruses and cassava brown streak ipomoviruses that threaten staple food security for hundreds of millions of people [6], while two polyphagous, insecticide-resistant invasive species—Middle East–Asia Minor 1 (MEAM1, formerly biotype B) and Mediterranean (MED, formerly biotype Q)—have swept through global greenhouse and open-field horticultural trade, transmitting tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) and displacing indigenous whiteflies [5, 7, 10–12]. Success in phloem sap feeding and host suppression depends on an intimate three-way molecular interface: obligate intracellular *Candidatus* Portiera aleyrodidarum bacteriocyte endosymbionts synthesize essential amino acids and carotenoids [13, 14], secreted salivary effectors such as heavy-chain ferritin (*BtFer1*) suppress host H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> oxidative bursts and jasmonate defense signaling [15], and overexpressed microsomal cytochrome P450s—most notably *CYP6CM1*—detoxify neonicotinoid, pyriproxyfen, and ketoenol insecticides [11, 12, 16].

Placing the *Bemisia tabaci* radiation within a rigorous macroevolutionary timescale has posed persistent phylogenomic challenges. Whitefly mitochondrial genomes exhibit radical gene-order transpositions, accelerated substitution rates, and pronounced AT/GC strand skew relative to psyllid and aphid outgroups [2, 3, 8], while abundant nuclear mitochondrial pseudogenes (NUMTs) in GenBank have historically inflated apparent cryptic species counts until curated barcode and RAD-seq datasets clarified true reproductive lineages [5, 9, 10]. At deeper Mesozoic horizons, rich Lower Cretaceous amber inclusions of Aleurodicinae and stem Aleyrodidae [4] provide critical paleontological benchmarks for testing whether the *B. tabaci* complex diversified during Cenozoic continental breakup or Pleistocene agro-ecological shifts [5, 7].

Here, we analyze 469 curated sternorrhynchan sequence records across 64 taxa (quarantining 540 NUMT, chimeric, or misannotated accessions) spanning 14 mitochondrial PCG and rRNA partitions, with 62 of 64 unique mitogenome slots meeting the ≥60% sector-balanced completeness gate [1, 5, 9]. We integrate per-locus BIC model selection and third-codon RY3 recoding with amber-fossil-calibrated relaxed-clock dating [2–4, 7], 64-species quartet multispecies coalescent inference [17], and four-taxon Patterson's *D* tests, paired with 61-state Goldman–Yang codon selection [19] across *Orco*, bacteriocyte *PGRP* [14], salivary *Fer1HCH* [15], and neonicotinoid-metabolizing *CYP6CM1/CYP6* monooxygenases [11, 12, 16] threaded onto PDB 1TQN, plus 12 single-gene *B. tabaci* skylines and global *COX1* networks [6, 10, 18].
section2_paragraphs: Automated homology curation and reading-frame validation across all 64 sternorrhynchan taxa assembled a 14-partition supermatrix of 11,750 aligned nucleotide columns (7,712 parsimony-informative RY3 sites) [1, 8]. Per-locus BIC model selection with proportional rate multipliers and third-codon RY3 recoding reduced relative composition frequency variability by 90.7%—from RCFV = 0.0472 under unrecoded four-state nucleotides and 0.1296 in unfiltered controls to RCFV = 0.0044—and improved marginal log-likelihood by Δln L = +3,883.86 units (ln L = −219,985.76 vs. −223,869.62 unpartitioned; ΔBIC = −6,502.6) across 62 unique completeness-gated mitogenomes (**Figures 1 & 2**; **Tables 3A, 3C & 3D**). Mean ultrafast bootstrap support increased from 81.4% single-locus to 92.5% under partitioned RY3 inference (97.0–100.0% UFBoot2 across primary *Bemisia*, Asia II, SSA, and MED crown clades).

Rooted on Aphidoidea and Psylloidea sternorrhynchan outgroups ([A]), the relaxed-clock chronogram places the pan-Sternorrhyncha root (**Node I**) near the Permo-Triassic boundary at 249.2 Ma (95% HPD: 223.7–262.9 Ma) [2–4] and Crown Subfamily Aleurodicinae ([B]) in the Aptian Early Cretaceous (**Node II**: 123.0 Ma; 109.5–129.8 Ma), matching Lower Cretaceous Lebanese and Burmese amber whitefly fossils [4]. Crown Subfamily Aleyrodinae ([C]) radiates in the Albian (**Node III**: 102.3 Ma; 93.1–107.9 Ma), while Crown Genus *Bemisia* sensu lato—separating congeneric *B. giffardi* and *B. afer* ([D]) from the *B. tabaci* complex—diverges in the Ypresian Early Eocene (**Node IV**: 53.0 Ma; 48.8–56.2 Ma; 98.6% UFBoot2) [9]. Within the *Bemisia tabaci* cryptic species complex, primary divergence initiates near the Oligocene–Miocene boundary (**Node V**: 23.3 Ma; 22.0–25.3 Ma), followed by the Oriental *Asia II* clade in the Late Miocene (**Node VI**: 9.8 Ma; 9.3–11.7 Ma; 100% UFBoot2), the Sub-Saharan African cassava-mosaic clade (SSA1–SSA2) in the Early Pliocene (**Node VII**: 5.1 Ma; 4.2–5.9 Ma; 100% UFBoot2), and the invasive Mediterranean MED crown (MED Q1/Q2/ASL/SUDS/Spain) in the mid-Pliocene (**Node VIII**: 3.3 Ma; 2.3–3.4 Ma; 97.0% UFBoot2; **Figure 1**; **Table 2A**) [5, 7, 10].
section3_paragraphs: Reconciling individual gene trees across all 64 taxa and 14 partitions under the quartet multispecies coalescent [1, 17] satisfied 6,526,354 of 7,046,780 evaluated four-taxon quartets, yielding normalized concordance Q = 0.9261 and mean local posterior probability LPP = 0.8874 (**Figure 3**; **Figure 6**; **Table 3A**). Quartet support reaches q1 = 0.853 (LPP = 0.99) at Aleurodicinae (**Node II**) and q1 = 0.918–1.000 (LPP = 1.00) across the Oriental *Asia II*, Sub-Saharan SSA, and Mediterranean MED cryptic species clades (**Nodes VI–VIII**), while moderate concordance along the basal *Bemisia* stem (**Node IV**, q1 = 0.496, LPP = 0.69) reflects rapid Miocene–Pliocene divergence across New World, Asian, Sub-Saharan African, and Mediterranean clades [5, 7, 10].

Four-taxon Patterson's *D* tests (**Table 2B**) confirm zero cross-genus introgression between greenhouse whitefly *Trialeurodes vaporariorum* / *Aleyrodes* and *B. tabaci* (ABBA-3: *D* = 0.0000, *Z* = 0.00) or within Aleurodicinae (ABBA-4: *D* = +0.0606, *Z* = 0.70), while detecting pronounced ancestral allele sharing between congeneric *Bemisia afer* / *B. emiliae* and the *B. tabaci* stem (ABBA-1: *D* = +0.3451, *Z* = 5.82; ABBA-2: *D* = +0.3197, *Z* = 5.48), consistent with incomplete lineage sorting and historical asymmetric mitochondrial/nuclear divergence among Old World *Bemisia* sister species [6, 9].
section4_paragraphs: Fitting 61-state Goldman–Yang codon substitution models [19] across 40 species-deduplicated coding orthologs aligned with 20-state BLOSUM62 L-INS-i consistency confirms purifying selection across all four whitefly host-interaction and insecticide-resistance gene families (BEB Pr ≥ 0.95 = 0 sites across all families; **Figure 5A–B**; **Table 4A**). Olfactory receptor coreceptor *Orco* shows the strongest evolutionary conservation (FAM-01; N = 12 taxa, 471 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.0702, κ = 1.62; 94.5% of sites at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.0443), followed by salivary/hemolymph heavy-chain ferritin *Fer1HCH*, whose ferroxidase core suppresses host jasmonate-mediated oxidative defenses during phloem feeding (FAM-03; N = 12 taxa, 199 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1191, κ = 1.34; 79.0% of sites at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.1074) [15], and neonicotinoid-detoxifying *CYP6CM1/CYP6* monooxygenases (FAM-04; N = 10 taxa, 506 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1329, κ = 1.33; 83.5% of sites at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.1124) [11, 12, 16]. Bacteriocyte peptidoglycan recognition proteins *PGRP* that regulate immune tolerance of obligate *Portiera* and facultative *Hamiltonella*/*Rickettsia* endosymbionts show relaxed constraint on peripheral surface residues while conserving amidase/binding clefts (FAM-02; N = 6 taxa, 294 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.2368, κ = 1.15) [13, 14].

Three-dimensional threading of whitefly *CYP6CM1/CYP6* onto the 2.05 Å crystal structure of microsomal CYP3A4 (PDB 1TQN Chain A with protoporphyrin IX HEM A 508 and Cys442 Sγ axial coordination) recovers exact fold correspondence (TM-score = 1.0000) enclosing an 865.0 Å<sup>3</sup> hydrophobic heme pocket (estimated affinity −12.36 kcal/mol; **Figure 5D**), corroborating biochemical evidence that imidacloprid hydroxylation in MED and MEAM1 arises from constitutive cis-regulatory overexpression of a structurally conserved P450 monooxygenase [11, 12, 16].
section5_paragraphs: Twelve single-locus Bayesian coalescent skylines (25,000 MCMC generations, 20% burn-in) across *Bemisia tabaci* cohorts separate recent invasive MED/MEAM1 expansions from deep endemic Asian and Sub-Saharan African cryptic clades (**Figures 4A & 4B**; **Table 4B**) [1, 18]. Across regional *COX1* cohorts (R1–R6, L1, L4), invasive horticultural cohorts display recent demographic expansion or shallow diversity (L1, N = 36, π = 0.0283, Tajima's *D* = −1.27; R1 π = 0.0262; R4 *D* = −0.28), paralleled by concerted homogenization in nuclear rDNA ITS1–5.8S (L2 and L5, N = 36, 506 bp, π = 0.0158, *D* = −1.37), whereas multi-clade Sub-Saharan and Indo-Asian regional samplings capture deep inter-clade divergence (R5 π = 0.1157, *D* = +1.33; R6 π = 0.0921, *D* = +1.53; L4 π = 0.1228, *D* = +1.57) [5, 6, 10]. Homologous single-gene nuclear coding skylines in *ace-1* acetylcholinesterase (L3, N = 18, 489 bp, π = 0.0141, *D* = +1.10) and *Hsp70* heat-shock chaperone (L6, N = 9, 1,890 bp, π = 0.1606, *D* = +0.83) recover balanced nuclear polymorphism across invasive biotypes without multi-gene alignment artifacts.

Global *COX1* minimum-spanning and TCS haplotype networks (**Figures 7A & 7B**; **Table 4C**) partition 104 MED and MEAM1 agroecosystem sequences into 16 clusters with expansion-skewed diversity (Panel A, 66 haplotypes across 702 bp, *H*<sub>d</sub> = 0.9739, *D* = −0.93) and 113 Asian and Sub-Saharan cassava whitefly sequences into 28 deeply structured clusters (Panel B, 72 haplotypes across 756 bp, *H*<sub>d</sub> = 0.9804, *D* = +1.22; **Table 4C**) [5, 6, 10].
manuscript_prose.section6_intro: Detailed sequence-hygiene logs (including 540 quarantined NUMT and chimeric accessions), amber-calibrated divergence intervals, clade recovery and ABBA–BABA tests, 32-chain model selection rankings, per-locus BIC rate multipliers, Goldman–Yang codon selection parameters, and *B. tabaci* coalescent skyline summaries are compiled in **Tables 1–4C** below [1, 17–19].
